text:
1,967,478,960 triangles at 60 fps in a desktop browser 🤯
three.js r187's MeshletDrawingPipeline splits meshes into 64-triangle clusters. the gpu culls the hidden ones and far stuff drops to coarser LODs.
BILLION, made with opus 5.5 #threejs #gamedev https://t.co/F8y3gjlrJb https://t.co/RcVED8MB5O
what_they_built: A browser scene that draws 1,967,478,960 triangles at 60 frames per second with three.js meshlets, made with Opus 5.5.

What came out: a mountain map, a glider that actually flies, a ruined tower, enemies that https://t.co/DT1pGwGEMB https://t.co/xwLtIFwEMk

text:
An airliner is many hidden systems working as one machine. I made a web app that x-rays one from gate to landing to show its fuel, hydraulics, electrics, engines and cabin air.

Built with Opus 5.5 using Blender + Three.js. Explore it live ↓ https://t.co/suPdUFa3P2
what_they_built: A web app that shows an airliner’s fuel, hydraulics, electrics, engines and cabin air from gate to landing, built with Opus 5.5, Blender and Three.js.

text:
i reverse engineered my Wi-Fi router with Claude Opus 5.5 and found a f*cking scary privacy problem...

every site I opened, my provider saw it. no encryption. just a readable list.

so I built a free open-source app that puts AI agents on watch over my network: Claude, ChatGPT https://t.co/WcYGFkxH3c https://t.co/3cF0vXQHBr
what_they_built: A free desktop app that scans a home network and lets Claude, ChatGPT or Grok answer questions about it, built with Claude Opus 5.5.
